Consult Summary:
- Young adult female with 2 days of gradually worsening, constant burning lower abdominal pain centered below the umbilicus, associated with pink-tinged urine, mild nausea, and subjective hot/sweats; clinician suspects urinary tract infection and started empiric antibiotics pending tests.

History:
- Presenting complaint:
  - Lower abdominal (below the belly button) constant burning/sore pain for ~2 days, worse on palpation and gradually increasing in severity.
  - Patient reports feeling hot and sweaty.
  - Pink-tinged urine noted; unsure if frank blood.
  - Mild nausea without vomiting.
  - Increased urinary frequency recently; patient attributes at least partly to increased fluid intake.
  - Recent constipation (since last week) that has since improved; bowel movements now normal.
- Timeline / progression:
  - Symptoms began approximately 2 days ago and have been gradually worsening.
  - Constipation occurred last week and has resolved.
- Exacerbating / relieving factors:
  - Pain is worse with pressure on the abdomen; no specific relieving factors reported.
  - Patient remains ambulatory and functioning.
- Associated symptoms / systems review:
  - Genitourinary: pink urine, increased frequency, no dysuria or stinging on voiding reported.
  - Gastrointestinal: mild nausea, no vomiting, no diarrhea, bowels now normal.
  - Constitutional: subjective feeling of being hot and sweaty; no measured fever reported.
  - Respiratory / Cardiovascular / Neurologic / Ophthalmic: denies shortness of breath, cough, palpitations, headaches, or vision changes.
- Gynecologic / sexual history:
  - Sexually active with a single partner; last sexual activity approximately 4 days ago.
  - On Implanon contraceptive implant placed ~1 year ago.
  - Last STD screen normal approximately 6 months ago.
  - Last menstrual period: patient first said ~3 weeks ago, then corrected to ~2 weeks ago (conflict noted — see Quality checks).
  - Patient acknowledges theoretical pregnancy risk if implant failed; clinician advised pregnancy test.

Past Medical History:
- Medical conditions:
  - No chronic medical conditions reported.
- Surgical history:
  - No prior surgeries.
- Medications:
  - Contraceptive implant: Implanon, inserted ~1 year ago.
  - No other regular medications reported.
- Allergies:
  - Not documented.

Social History:
- Living situation:
  - Lives in a share house with two roommates.
- Occupation:
  - Accountant.
- Tobacco:
  - Denies smoking.
- Alcohol:
  - Drinks socially; no excess reported.
- Illicit drugs:
  - Not mentioned.

Family History:
- No relevant family history reported or known.

Physical Examination:
- Vitals:
  - Not documented in the transcript.
- Exam findings:
  - No physical examination findings documented in the transcript.

Investigations:
- Tests discussed / planned (no results recorded):
  - Urine testing (urinalysis / urine culture) discussed as initial tests to evaluate for urinary tract infection.
  - Pregnancy test recommended to exclude pregnancy as a cause/contributor.
  - Clinician indicated ability to organize tests but no test results documented.

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1: Suspected urinary tract infection (provisional)
  - Assessment:
    - Clinical presentation consistent with possible UTI: lower abdominal pain, pink-tinged urine, increased urinary frequency, mild nausea, subjective feverishness.
  - Plan:
    - Empiric antibiotic therapy prescribed: Trimethoprim.
      - Dosing in transcript contains conflicting phrasing: "you can take two tablets" and "one tablet twice a day for three days" (conflict noted). Medication name and dosing/route/frequency from transcript recorded under Quality checks.
    - Encourage oral fluids.
    - Recommend symptomatic analgesia: Paracetamol as needed.
    - Advise cranberry juice may help urine symptoms (patient advised to try).
    - Return or contact clinician if symptoms worsen (worsening abdominal pain, persistent fever/hotness, vomiting) or do not improve within a few days.
- Issue 2: Lower abdominal pain of uncertain etiology (differential includes gastrointestinal causes)
  - Assessment:
    - Pain localized below the umbilicus, gradual onset and worsening; alternative etiologies possible (gastrointestinal).
  - Plan:
    - Arrange initial investigations (urine testing and pregnancy test) to help delineate cause.
    - Reassess in clinic if symptoms persist or worsen.
- Issue 3: Possible pregnancy (implant failure unlikely but possible)
  - Assessment:
    - Patient on Implanon; reports unprotected sex with same partner; menstrual timing uncertain.
  - Plan:
    - Obtain pregnancy test to exclude pregnancy prior to or during treatment course.

General plan items:
- Organize/perform urinalysis and pregnancy test (no results yet).
- Start empiric Trimethoprim as above.
- Symptomatic care: Paracetamol and fluids; consider cranberry juice.
- Follow-up: Return in a few days if not improving or sooner if worsening.

document_quality / Quality checks:

  - Allergies not documented.
  - Complete medication reconciliation not documented (only Implanon reported).
  - Vital signs not documented.

  - Results of requested investigations (urinalysis, urine culture, pregnancy test) not available.
- Internal conflicts from the transcript:
  - Trimethoprim dosing: transcript states both "you can take two tablets" and "one tablet twice a day for three days" (conflict noted).
  - Last menstrual period timing: patient initially said "about three weeks ago" then corrected to "two weeks ago" (conflict noted).
- Transcript quality:
  - Overall clear and audible; minimal hesitations. Several management recommendations and testing plans discussed, but no documented physical exam or investigation results in the transcript.
